title: Mini Toolkit
goal: In this lesson you will build a tiny toolkit that mixes import styles and useful tools.
learn: Choose between import and from import
Put together a small multi-tool script
idea: Mini toolkit time. Combine import math, import random, and maybe from math import sqrt for a favorite. Always call random.seed(1) in lesson demos. Print a short menu of results so it feels like a pocket utility.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change sqrt(36) to sqrt(49) and press Run. That line should show 7.0.

practice.text: Build a 3-line toolkit printout: sqrt(16), a seeded dice roll, and math.pi rounded to 2 decimals.
practice.hint: Line 1 is print(sqrt(16)). Line 2 is print(random.randint(1, 6)) after seed(1). Line 3 is print(round(math.pi, 2)).
practice.starterTip: Expect 4.0, then dice 2, then 3.14 when you Run with the starter imports and seed(1).
practice.starter:
import math
import random
from math import sqrt
random.seed(1)
print()
print()
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if 4.0, dice 2, and 3.14 style pi appear with seed(1).

practice.text: from math import floor. import random; seed(1); print floor of a random.randint(5,15)/2.
practice.hint: Inside print(), use floor(...) around random.randint(5, 15) / 2. floor rounds down to a whole number.
practice.starterTip: Try print(floor(random.randint(5, 15) / 2)). seed(1) keeps the roll predictable for checking.
practice.starter:
from math import floor
import random
random.seed(1)
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if seed(1) used and floor of roll/2 prints a number.

quiz.question: What belongs in a mini toolkit lesson?

options.text: A few imported tools working together

quiz.correct: Right, a small combo of tools is all it takes.

quiz.question: Must every tool use from import?
quiz.correct: Yes, both styles are fine, so pick whatever reads clearly.

quiz.question: What should you do before practice rolls?
quiz.correct: Right, the seed keeps the checks fair.

project.title: Pocket Toolkit
project.desc: Print a banner, and then sqrt(81), ceil(2.2), two seeded dice rolls, and round(pi, 2). Use seed(1).
